description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-11 by code inspection + a live parse of ENDF/B-VIII.0 graphite.

STATE: src/thermr/scattering.rs is the documented 'hand-off' surface that outram-mc-libs consumes, but it exposes exactly one type, IncoherentInelasticScattering, covering MF=7/MT=4 only. The two ELASTIC channels are implemented as bare impl blocks on the raw parser structs:
  - CoherentElastic::cross_section / ::bragg_reflections  (src/thermr/coherent.rs:29,53)
  - IncoherentElastic::cross_section / ::equiprobable_cosines / ::debye_waller  (src/thermr/incoherent_elastic.rs:36,64,83)
Neither has a uom-typed, temperature-selecting, pre-tabulated consumer struct analogous to IncoherentInelasticScattering, and grep shows the ONLY in-tree consumer of either is src/acer/thermal.rs (the ACE writer). No transport crate can reach them through the documented surface.

WHY IT MATTERS (HTR-10 critical path): graphite (tsl-crystalline-graphite MAT=30, tsl-reactor-graphite-10P MAT=31, -30P MAT=32) is coherent-elastic + incoherent-inelastic, with NO incoherent-elastic (verified: parse_mf7 reports coherent_elastic=true, incoherent_elastic=false, incoherent_inelastic=true for all three). Coherent elastic is ~90% of graphite thermal scattering at 0.0253 eV. So the one channel that dominates the HTR-10 moderator is the one with no consumer surface.

WORK: add a CoherentElasticScattering consumer struct in thermr::scattering mirroring IncoherentInelasticScattering — from_endf_file(path, mat, temperature), uom-typed cross_section(E), and a sample-a-Bragg-reflection method returning (E_out = E_in, mu) from bragg_reflections' (mu, weight) pairs. Do the same for IncoherentElastic (needed later for ZrH, not for graphite). Depends on op-1y4y for correct temperature behaviour.

SIZE: small. The physics is already implemented and tested; this is a typed wrapper + temperature selection.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: DONE 2026-08-11 (this session; unverified-by-human, not committed yet). thermr::scattering now exposes all three channels: CoherentElasticScattering (from_endf_file/from_tape at a uom Temperature; uom cross_section(E) per principal atom; bragg_cutoff() = first edge with nonzero S, 1.8223 meV for graphite; bragg_reflections(E) normalised-probability (mu,p) list, zero-weight grid points filtered; sample(E, xi)->(E_out=E_in, mu) with caller-owned RNG) and IncoherentElasticScattering (cross_section(E), equiprobable_cosines(E,nbin); constructor refuses temps outside the W'(T) table range) alongside IncoherentInelasticScattering. All re-exported from thermr. Temperature resolution at construction per the shared mf7 policy (tolerance/interpolate/refuse). Consumer-surface consistency V&V in tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs passes (surface == mf7-level to machine precision; probabilities sum to 1; sampling elastic). Downstream MC wiring (op-nhoa/op-hc2o) untouched per scope.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
One addition to this surface, 2026-08-11 (uncommitted), made while implementing op-nhoa: CoherentElasticScattering::bragg_edge_table() -> Vec<(NeutronEnergy, CrossSection)>, one uom-typed pair per tabulated Bragg edge (221 for ENDF/B-VIII.0 crystalline graphite), where sigma_i = S(E_i,T)/(E_i*natom) is the value cross_section() takes throughout [E_i, E_{i+1}).

WHY IT WAS NEEDED: sigma_coh_el(E) is a 1/E sawtooth with a discontinuity at every edge. A consumer that pre-tabulates it on its own log grid - which outram-mc must do, to keep the transport hot loop cheap - smears all 221 edges. Exposing the step table lets the consumer cache the channel EXACTLY instead: measured worst relative deviation of outram-mc's cached copy vs this surface is 7.67e-16 over 21199 points from 1e-4 to 4 eV, and the whole table is ~3.5 kB, cheaper than the resample it replaces. Everything else (the cumulative structure factor S_i/natom = sigma_i*E_i, and each edge's sampling weight as its increment) is recoverable from the pairs exactly.

It mirrors the CoherentElasticXS::bragg_edges() / ::factors() pair that OpenMC's CoherentElasticAE::sample consumes (src/secondary_thermal.cpp:34-54), so it is a port move rather than an invention. No behaviour change to any existing method. njoy full suite green after it (393 lib tests + all integration, scripts/test.sh, release). Not closing - human review still owed on this bead's original work too.

title: njoy THERMR: no consumer surface for the thermal ELASTIC channels — thermr::scattering exposes incoherent-inelastic only

description:
The substrate that makes the aesthetic bar achievable, and the missing abstraction today. PipeVisual currently takes screen_position: Pos2 + screen_vector: Vec2 in raw SCREEN POINTS, hardcodes PIPE_STROKE_WIDTH = 4.0, and has no elevation and no connection concept -- so every endpoint is hand-placed by the app and nothing about the drawing is derived.

Needed: a layout module owning a plant-space (metres, with elevation) -> screen transform plus a node graph, so components are placed at real coordinates and connected by node. Pipe direction/length then follow from real geometry, connections are shared nodes (so runs meet smoothly), and elevation makes natural-circulation loops read correctly.

tampines::components::Pipe ALREADY exposes everything needed -- diameter: Length, length: Length, inclination: Angle, roughness: Length (crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:37-43), all uom-typed and stable (step() is inert, so they are caller-supplied and trustworthy). No tampines change required for pipes.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION, deferred by the maintainer (2026-08-04) -- resolve before building: is stroke width proportional to DIAMETER (a true scale drawing; bore area then reads correctly to the eye as width^2) or to AREA (width proportional to d^2, exaggerating large pipes)? Note also that bores (~0.05 m) and runs (~10 m) cannot share one scale or pipes render as invisible hairlines, so diameter needs its own exaggerated scale -- which must be documented honestly as exaggeration, not as proportionality. The V&V write-up has to state which convention is used.
title: Widget Studio: plant-space layout layer — metres to screen transform, node graph, elevation
